newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity names two to head investment strategy.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity names two to head investment strategy.

text.p: Fidelity Investments portfolio managers Richard Habermann and Jonathan Weed Tuesday were named to joint Chief Investment Strategists for Portfolio Advisory Services, the unit that provides professional investment management of clients' portfolios of Fidelity mutual funds.
The two men succeed Robert Beckwitt who is leaving Fidelity to join Goldman Sachs effective Sept 1.

For a minimum investment of $200,000, advisory services provides investors with tailored investment management for a diversified portfolio of Fidelity mutual funds, the nation's largest mutual fund company said in a statement.

Habermann heads the newly formed Asset Allocation Group, which in addition to Weed, also includes George Vanderheiden, manager of the Destiny and Fidelity Advisor Growth Opportunities funds and Michael Gray, manager of the Fidelity Intermiddent Bond Fund.
Before taking over as lead manager of Fidelity's Asset Manager funds, Habermann was division head for international equity funds and was involved with these funds' asset allocation strategies.

Weed, who joined Fidelity in 1984, had been assisting Beckwitt with the management of the advisory services. He help originate Fidelity asset allocation discipline and also managed the company's $2 billion equity index mutual funds for more than five years.
